shell.emptyHint: Plug in a console cable, or press {{shortcut}} to connect.

quick.label: Quick connect
quick.hint: Type ssh admin@10.0.0.1, telnet 10.0.0.5 2001, COM4 or a saved session name
quick.noMatch: No saved session or serial port named “{{text}}”.

status.rxTxHint: Bytes received / sent in this tab

health.noData: Cable connected but no data. The device may be off.

errors.portNotFound: {{port}} was not found. Is the cable plugged in?
errors.db: Could not save: the local database is unavailable.
errors.protocolNotSupported: Only serial sessions can be opened in this version.
errors.connectionRefused: {{port}} refused the connection. Is the service enabled on that port?
errors.timeout: {{port}} did not answer in time. The host may be down or filtered.
errors.authFailed: Login failed: user name or password was rejected.
errors.hostKeyChanged: Connection blocked: the SSH host key of {{port}} has changed. If the device was replaced, forget the stored key.
errors.noCommonAlgorithm: No common SSH algorithm with {{port}}. For older devices enable “Legacy algorithms” in the session.
errors.badPassword: Wrong master password, or the file is damaged.

identity.breakHint: Send a serial BREAK signal (e.g. to enter ROMMON)
identity.device: Device (from the prompt and version output)

tabs.label: Open sessions
tabs.alreadyOpen: {{port}} is already open in a tab.
tabs.splitNeedsTab: Open another tab to split the view
tabs.splitFull: Split view holds up to 4 panes
tabs.detachNeedsSession: This tab has no live session to move
tabs.detachDuringLogin: Finish the login before moving the tab
tabs.detachFailed: Could not move the tab to a new window
tabs.dropOutside: Release to open in a new window
tabs.dragHint: Drag tabs to reorder, onto a pane to split, or out of the window to detach

terminal.dropped: — {{size}} of older output skipped while this tab was hidden —

library.bulkUserHint: Empty removes it. Serial sessions are skipped.
library.bulkDeleted: {{count}} sessions deleted. Saved passwords were removed.
library.bulkHint: ⌘/Ctrl-click or Shift-click to select several sessions

consoles.driverMissing: {{chip}} detected, but its driver does not seem to be installed.

editor.name: Name
editor.legacyAlgorithmsHint: For old Cisco/Ruijie/Juniper devices: also offers diffie-hellman-group1/14-sha1, ssh-rsa, CBC ciphers and hmac-sha1.
editor.useAgentHint: Tries up to 2 keys from ssh-agent / Pageant before the password. Network devices often allow only 3 attempts.
editor.jumpHint: Connects to this SSH server first, then to the device through it (user@host:port).
editor.forwardsHint: One per line: L listen:host:port (local), R listen:host:port (remote), D listen (SOCKS5). Local ports listen on 127.0.0.1 only.
editor.autoCommandsHint: One per line, sent when the device is idle at its prompt (after you log in). Do not put passwords here.
editor.lineHint: Line levels after the port opens. Some console cables or devices need DTR or RTS off.
editor.identify: Read the device identity after login
editor.identifyHint: Runs a read-only show version once in the background; its output never appears in the terminal.

panel.label: Side panel
panel.notesEmpty: Notes for the device you are connected to will appear here.
panel.analyzerEmpty: Command output analysis will appear here.
panel.snippetsEmpty: Reusable command snippets will appear here.

settings.stripeHint: The colored stripe next to every terminal.
settings.languageHint: System follows your operating system language.
settings.hotplugToast: Notify when a console cable is plugged in
settings.hotplugToastHint: A quiet notification with a Connect button. No sound.
settings.autoReconnectHint: Sessions waiting for an unplugged cable continue automatically.
settings.netAutoReconnectHint: After a timeout or network error, retries after 2, 5, 10 and 30 seconds. Never after you log out or when login fails.
settings.logEnabledHint: Device output is streamed to a file; what you type (passwords) is never logged.
settings.logTemplateHint: {name}, {date}, {time} are replaced; existing files are never overwritten.
settings.pasteDelayHint: Serial and Telnet only, so the device buffer does not overflow. 0 = off.
settings.lineTimestampsHint: Shown in the terminal only; the device output is unchanged.
settings.fontFamilyHint: Empty = JetBrains Mono (bundled). Any installed monospaced font, e.g. "Cascadia Mono".
settings.cursorBlinkHint: Off by default: a steady cursor lets the CPU idle.
settings.identifyHint: Read-only show version once per connection, hidden from the terminal. Can be turned off per session.

ssh.forgetHostKeyHint: Only if you know the device was replaced or re-keyed. The next connection stores the new key.

log.openFailed: The session log could not be created; the session continues without it.

credentials.ownLogin: This session's own user and password
credentials.passwordSaved: Saved in keychain — type to replace
credentials.passwordOptional: Optional — asked when connecting if empty
credentials.keychainHint: Passwords are kept only in the system keychain, never in KenShell files or logs.
credentials.saveFailed: The password could not be saved to the keychain.
credentials.profilesHint: A login profile (user + password) can be used by many sessions. Changing it here updates all of them.
credentials.name: Name

data.importHint: Each source goes into its own folder; sessions that already exist there are skipped. Passwords are never imported.
data.exportHint: All folders and sessions, without passwords.
data.vaultHint: Sessions, folders, credential profiles, known SSH hosts and saved passwords in one file, encrypted with a master password (Argon2id + ChaCha20-Poly1305). Key files are not included. A lost master password cannot be recovered.

keys.generateHint: Ed25519 is recommended; older devices may need RSA. OpenSSH keys also get a .pub file next to them. Private key files are readable only by you.
keys.convertHint: Opens OpenSSH, PuTTY (.ppk v2/v3) and PEM keys. The public key is shown without the passphrase.
keys.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard

details.title: Details · {{name}}
details.noDevice: Nothing known yet: the device is identified after login.

colors.modesHint: Colour and label of each CLI mode, for every vendor. Applies to both themes.
colors.vendorHint: Different colours for one vendor; empty rows use the mode colours above.

notes.placeholder: Note… Enter adds, Shift+Enter new line. "Gi1/0/24: camera" links to the interface.
notes.onDevice: Saved to the device (same notes over SSH or console)
notes.onSession: Saved to the session; moves to the device once it is identified
notes.noTab: Open a session to see its notes.
notes.needsSession: Notes need a saved session or an identified device.
